_comment: One morning of a forwarder's inbound mail - SYNTHETIC, authored like the bookings. The workflow layer (src/workflow.py) reads it the way the risk layer reads a scenario: the input is authored, everything done with it is computed on the run. Messages refer to bookings by the carrier booking reference, the way real mail does; the Inbox Worker has to link them. Two mistakes are planted on purpose so the learning loop has something to learn from: IN-104 and IN-109 say 'booking' more often than 'quote' and are really rate requests, and IN-102 and IN-107 carry a German weight label the extractor does not know. Nothing here is a real customer, carrier contact or document.

rate_sheet._comment: Synthetic reference rates, EUR per container, for pricing a quote. Not market rates. A route's cost_index (100 = baseline) scales the base, so the routes file stays the one source of relative cost.
